criteria.reasoning: The report only gives the year of death, "Agnes Gund (1938–2025)" and "Advanced age at time of death (2025)". It never dates it to September (18/19) 2025. It also treats her as living elsewhere, e.g. "She is not a transactional donor", "May prefer: Selling assets instead of cash gifts" and "Competes with her own institution".
Section 2 states "Family wealth origin: Banking fortune via Cleveland Trust (father George Gund II)." That names George Gund II as the source of the family fortune.
The report states she "served as President of Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) from 1991–2002 and remained President Emerita and Life Trustee." Those are the correct years and roles.
The report states "In 1977, she founded Studio in a School, specifically to address cuts in NYC public-school arts funding." The year is right and the credit goes to her.

The report lists "$100M → Art for Justice Fund (2017)", "Seeded from sale of Roy Lichtenstein painting", and gives the sale as "$165M", which it says "triggered above gift". The painting is not named, but none of the FAIL conditions apply: no other painting or artist is named, the commitment is $100M rather than the full sale price, and the year is 2017.

The fund appears only as her past initiative ("~$22M+ in early grants", "mirrors her Art for Justice framing"). The report never says it is operating now and never recommends approaching it as a funder.
The report never names the AG Foundation, Catherine Gund or Anna Traggio.
The report gives no dollar figure for Gund's or the AG Foundation's grants to Studio in a School. It mentions the organisation only as something she founded.
The report gives no AG Foundation size figures at all, so no stale figure is presented as current.

Under Potential Red Flags it lists "Competing loyalty: Strong, lifelong commitment to Studio in a School. May prioritize existing institution over new ones". The Bottom Line repeats "Competes with her own institution." Together these draw the competitive implication for the requesting program.

Section 6 sets a "Primary ask: $5M–$10M" and a "Stretch ask: $15M–$25M" with an engagement strategy aimed at her ("Direct continuation of her own legacy"). The closing pitch is addressed to her: "Scale what you started". This proposes soliciting Agnes Gund herself.
The report does not mention the AG Foundation and does not recommend any unsolicited application or letter of inquiry to it.
The report does not mention or recommend the George Gund Foundation as a funding source.
The report credits her with none of her brothers' gifts or roles: no Kenyon gallery, no Foundation Fighting Blindness co-founding and no sports-team ownership.

The fact sheet states that, being dead, she "cannot be cultivated or solicited". The report nonetheless sets a "Primary ask: $5M–$10M" for her. It also describes her in the present tense as a prospect who "Competes with her own institution" and "May prefer: Selling assets instead of cash gifts", which contradicts her status.
